ri.rcode:
library(lme4)
m <- lmer(Reaction ~ Days + (1 | Subject), data = sleepstudy)

# the ICC this page reports, straight from the model object
performance::icc(m)

# the 95% intervals shown above (estimate +/- 1.96 * SE)
confint(m, method = "Wald")

# better intervals when the call is close (slower, no df needed)
confint(m, method = "profile")

# p-values, if you want them: lmerTest adds Satterthwaite df
library(lmerTest)
m2 <- lmer(Reaction ~ Days + (1 | Subject), data = sleepstudy)
summary(m2)

rs.rcode:
library(lme4)
m <- lmer(Reaction ~ Days + (Days | Subject), data = sleepstudy)

# the ICC this page reports, straight from the model object
performance::icc(m)
#> this model has a random slope, so performance::icc() averages the
#> random-effect variance over your observed predictor values. It needs
#> the data, so it will differ from the at-zero ICC shown on this page.

# the 95% intervals shown above (estimate +/- 1.96 * SE)
confint(m, method = "Wald")

# better intervals when the call is close (slower, no df needed)
confint(m, method = "profile")

# p-values, if you want them: lmerTest adds Satterthwaite df
library(lmerTest)
m2 <- lmer(Reaction ~ Days + (Days | Subject), data = sleepstudy)
summary(m2)

glmer.rcode:
library(lme4)
m <- glmer(r2 ~ Anger + Gender + btype + (1 | id), family = binomial, data = VerbAgg)

# the ICC this page reports, straight from the model object
performance::icc(m)

# the 95% intervals shown above (estimate +/- 1.96 * SE)
confint(m, method = "Wald")

# Profile intervals are better when the call is close, but on a glmer fit
# profiling often stops with "profiling detected new, lower deviance" if the
# optimiser did not land exactly on the optimum. Refit with a tighter
# tolerance first, or stay with the Wald intervals above.
# confint(m, method = "profile")
